Planned retire.note:
Planned retirement year.

Source:
- The PNM 2026 resource plan, filed September 1, 2026, at https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2026-irp_final_report_only_sc-pdf says on PDF page 170, in the list of reasons the capacity need grows, "Retirements of Afton, Luna, and Rio Bravo by end of 2044". PDF page 177 repeats that all other existing gas units "remain in service through 2044".

What changed:
- The existing record gives 2039, from the PNM 2023 resource plan at https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2023-irp-final-pdf on PDF page 96, in the section Rio Bravo Generating Station, which says the plant is available "through 2039, the plant's planned retirement year". The 2026 plan replaces that date with the end of 2044.
- The September 2026 EIA-860M table at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx shows no planned retirement year for this unit.

The human adds a new scheduled retirement event with Event Year 2044 and Source Year 2026, and does not change the 2039 event.

Status.note:
The unit is still operating.

Source:
- The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx, sheet Operating, plant 55039, generator GT1, reads status OP Operating, nameplate 150.0 MW, operating April 2000, owner entity Public Service Co of NM.
- The PNM 2026 resource plan at https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2026-irp_final_report_only_sc-pdf lists Rio Bravo as a 149 MW combustion turbine in its table of current resources, around PDF page 4360 of the extracted text, and says on PDF page 170 it retires by the end of 2044. No retirement, mothballing or sale was announced.

Backup Power.note:
Backup Power stays no.

Source:
- The PNM 2023 resource plan at https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2023-irp-final-pdf, PDF page 96, section Rio Bravo Generating Station, calls the plant a natural gas-fired generating plant that serves as "an important PNM load-side generating resource" for transmission support. It is a utility peaker on the PNM grid, not a backup supply for a single site.
- No document states the words backup power for this plant, so this rests on how the plant is described. That is why this is rated medium.

units.notes: Rio Bravo GT1 is still operating. The planned retirement year moves from 2039 to 2044 in PNM's 2026 resource plan. No owner change was found; the owner in the EIA table is PNM's operating company.

source_log.note: Plant 55039 generator GT1 operating, 150.0 MW, no planned retirement.
The harvest lead is a county packet about a nearby solar and battery site and does not concern this plant's status. Not opened further.
